turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Krishnan sir, come and sit. I will check the pressure and the pulse before doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, sister. My wife only forced me to come. It is a check-up, that is all, nothing is wrong as such.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Arm loose, please. Blood pressure is one hundred and fifty-two over ninety-four. Pulse eighty-four. Oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): One fifty-two? That is high, no? At home it shows one thirty something and then I think the machine is faulty. Is your machine correct?
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He fights with the home machine every day. They are calling us, come.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sit down. What brings you?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Just a check-up, doctor. I am sixty-three. My wife said at this age we should not wait for a problem to—
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain. I am fine in that sense. I only wanted to ask if my BP tablet dose is—
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ramesh. The stairs. You promised you would tell him.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not pain, doctor. When I climb to the second floor, or if I walk fast to the bus stop, there is a tight squeezing in the centre of the chest. If I stop and stand for a minute it goes. Walking slowly, nothing comes.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has this tightness been there?
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He will wander off, just wait.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Around two three months. Not every day. Some weeks nothing at all. Is a heart attack coming? I am very frightened, kindly tell me straight.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Breathlessness along with it?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Breathing is normal.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sweating? Does the feeling go to the left arm or the jaw?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No sweating. It does not spread anywhere. So it can be gas, no? Acidity also feels like this, I was reading.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Palpitations? Giddiness?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neither. If this needs angiography, is that a very big thing? My neighbour had it and he was—
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): We are not talking angiography. Are you on treatment for blood pressure?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Since about eight years. That tablet I take daily, I don't miss it.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Known hypertension. Which tablet, what strength?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine. Five milligram, one in the morning after breakfast. For the pressure.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And aspirin. Small white one. He takes it only when he feels like, not the way they told him.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Aspirin — dose, and how often were you advised?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-five milligram. At the camp they said every day. I manage two times a week, sometimes three. I forget. Is missing it dangerous? Should I stop it before any test?
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do not stop it. From tonight, aspirin seventy-five every day, after food. Amlodipine you continue, same dose, every morning.

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Both together is safe? I saw a video that aspirin makes you bleed. And I already drank tea and ate two biscuits, so if you want fasting tests I have spoiled it. I am getting more tense now.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any other medicines?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only these two.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke? Alcohol?

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I never smoked. I don't take alcohol. I am retired, accounts section in the Port Trust, sitting work mostly. Can tension itself give this tightness? I keep worrying about my—
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he doesn't sleep. Wakes at three and stares at the fan.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am asking him, not you. Is sleep a problem?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): A little only. I wake early and the mind keeps running. Not every night. The chest thing is different, no?
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me check. Heart sounds are normal. Lungs are clear. No swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Then nothing serious, yes? Why send tests? Will you admit me? There is a family function, I cannot stay in hospital, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): For a plain check-up I will skip the ECG. Give routine bloods next week, whenever you are free. No hurry.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Next week he will cancel. I have watched him stop on the stairs and hold the railing.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Not every time. Only if I hurry. Maybe I made it sound big. Is ECG painful? How long it takes? I am a little shaky about machines.

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hold on. With this stair tightness I am changing that. ECG today, here. Bloods today for lipid profile and creatinine. You have had tea, so no fasting sugar today. Come back one morning, nothing to eat, and we will do the sugar.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing to eat from when? And the ECG, five minutes or one hour? Sister does it? Kindly tell me what all to avoid. I will follow, I just need to know.

[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): ECG is about five minutes, stickers only, no pain, the nurse will do it. Night before the sugar test, nothing by mouth after dinner. Till we have the reports, do not rush on the stairs. If the tightness starts while you are resting, or you get sweating and breathlessness with it, go to emergency. Don't wait for me.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Resting means sitting also? And tonight the aspirin, full seventy-five after food, yes? Will the BP tablet damage the kidney? That is why creatinine, no?

[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, creatinine is the kidney test, sensible while you are on amlodipine. Take the aspirin after food tonight and daily after that. This tightness on effort, easing when you stop, may be angina. I will not confirm that from talk alone.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Angina means the heart, then. If the ECG is normal am I out of danger? You won't put me on the treadmill, no? My knee also—

[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am not booking a treadmill. We look at this ECG and these bloods first. I want you back in one week, with the reports, and you come fasting that morning so the sugar is drawn then.
[SEG0049] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, the ECG machine is free. Shall I take him now and send the bloods after?
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. ECG now. Lipid profile and creatinine now. Not the fasting glucose. Review in one week, fasting.

[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Sister, the shirt has to come off, yes? Doctor, one week feels very long. What if the tightness comes tomorrow morning? Should my wife stay in the house with me? I cannot keep my thoughts straight.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Shirt off, yes. One week stands. She can stay if you both want. Pain at rest, you go to emergency, you don't sit and discuss it.
[SEG0053] person_1 (NURSE): Come, sir. Machine is just here. It will not hurt.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): I am coming. Doctor, you will explain the reports yourself, no? I don't want to only see numbers and worry.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

bad.reason: Aspirin 75 mg is supported, but patient reported taking it only 2-3 times weekly, not daily.
bad.text: Aspirin (generic_name=aspirin, dose=75 mg, frequency=once daily, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Hypertension and about 8 years are supported, but duration was reported by patient, not doctor.

omissions.text: Patient denied chest pain when specifically asked.
Amlodipine dosing details are incomplete: patient said 5 mg one tablet in the morning after breakfast; record only says once daily.
Aspirin use is recorded wrongly as currently once daily; patient said he had been advised 75 mg daily but was actually taking it only two times a week, sometimes three, because he forgets.
Doctor explicitly advised not to stop aspirin before any test.
Patient denied taking any other medicines besides amlodipine and aspirin.
Sleep problem history included waking at 3 a.m. per family member, and patient confirmed mild early waking with mind running, not every night.
Doctor initially said he would skip the ECG and do routine bloods next week with no hurry, but then changed plan after family input to ECG today and bloods today.
Family member reported she had watched him stop on the stairs and hold the railing.
Fasting blood sugar was deferred because patient had already had tea and two biscuits that day.
ECG was explained as about five minutes, stickers only, no pain, and to be done by the nurse.
Doctor instructed patient to come back in one week with the reports and to come fasting that morning so the sugar is drawn then.
Doctor warned that if pain/tightness occurs at rest, the patient should go to emergency and not sit and discuss it.
